title: Reachability
description: Can everything reach everything, and how fast? Ping, health URLs, the public Kubeletto path, the internet and the router's DNS. Open it after HostUnreachable, HttpProbeFailed, InternetDown, DnsResolverFailing, KubelettoPublicPathDown or RemoteAccessDown to see which probe fails and since when.

panels.title: Critical hosts down
panels.description: Critical-tier hosts that do not answer ping (rule HostUnreachable, severity critical: 3 minutes). Any red is act-now. Tier comes from each host's monitoring block in inventory/lab.yaml. Whole fleet, not filtered by the Host variable.

panels.title: Standard hosts down
panels.description: Standard-tier hosts that do not answer ping (rule HostUnreachable, severity warning: 3 minutes). Best-effort hosts are not counted: `ai` is an on-demand VM that is off most of the time, which is expected, and k3s-worker is info-only.

panels.title: Internet
panels.description: Ping to 1.1.1.1 or 8.8.8.8 from the monitoring CT (rule InternetDown: both fail for 3 minutes). DOWN means the household uplink is out and Telegram cannot be reached; the alert arrives afterwards as a record.

panels.title: Admin gateways up
panels.description: How many of the two Tailscale subnet routers (admin-gw on pve3, admin-gw2 on pve2) answer ping. 2 is healthy; 1 is HostUnreachable at warning (the pair fails over); 0 is rule RemoteAccessDown (critical, 3 minutes): no remote access to the lab at all.

panels.title: Health URLs failing
panels.description: Health URLs from inventory/lab.yaml that do not answer as expected (rule HttpProbeFailed: 5 minutes, severity from the host's tier). The host still pings when this is red, so the service, not the machine, is the problem.

panels.title: Kubeletto public path
panels.description: api.kubeletto.com/healthz and the registry token endpoint, probed through the public edge as a customer would (rule KubelettoPublicPathDown: 5 minutes). Catches a broken DNS record, tunnel or Cloudflare setting that the in-lab checks cannot see.

panels.title: DNS resolver
panels.description: The hEX resolver (10.10.10.1) answers a lookup of a public name (rule DnsResolverFailing: 3 minutes, critical). Red means every lab VLAN has lost name resolution even if the internet itself is up.

panels.title: Soonest certificate expiry
panels.description: Days until the soonest TLS certificate seen by the HTTP probes expires, management UIs and the public Kubeletto endpoints (anything beyond a year reads 365). No alert rule watches this: it is a review item. Under 30 days is worth a look, under 14 is urgent.

panels.title: Ping state per host
panels.description: Whether each host answers ping, over time (the HostUnreachable condition; it fires after 3 minutes down). Green = up, red = down. Blue = a best-effort host (`ai`, k3s-worker) that is down: `ai` is an on-demand VM, off most of the time, so blue there is expected. A hole that spans several hosts on one node means that node, not the hosts.

targets.expr: probe_success{job="blackbox_icmp", role!="internet", tier!="best-effort", instance=~"$instance"} or (1 + (probe_success{job="blackbox_icmp", role!="internet", tier="best-effort", instance=~"$instance"} == bool 0))

panels.title: Ping round-trip time
panels.description: Round-trip time of the ping to each host that answers. On the lab LAN this is under 5 ms; a host that jumps to 20 ms or more has a congested or flapping path (the switch and valkey have shown spikes of 22 to 25 ms). Down hosts are left out (their RTT reads 0). No alert rule watches latency.

panels.title: Availability, last 7 days
panels.description: Share of the last 7 days each host answered ping. Green is 99.9 % or better, orange under 99.9 %, red under 99 % (a host down for more than 100 minutes a week). Best-effort hosts are left out (`ai` is on demand, so it would always read near 0 %). A guest that was stopped on purpose also lowers its bar.

panels.title: Public probes: up or down
panels.description: The two probes through the public edge: api.kubeletto.com/healthz and the registry token endpoint (rule KubelettoPublicPathDown: either down for 5 minutes). The token endpoint returns 401 to an anonymous request on purpose and the probe counts that as up. Red means customers cannot deploy or call the API.

panels.title: Public path availability, 7 days
panels.description: Share of the last 7 days each public probe answered correctly. Green is 99.9 % or better, orange under 99.9 %, red under 99 %. The probe runs every 60 s, so 1 % is about 100 minutes. A dip here that the in-lab health URLs do not show suggests the household uplink or Cloudflare rather than the cluster.

panels.title: Public probe time
panels.description: Total time of each public probe, from the monitoring CT out through the household line and back. Duration of the customer-facing path: the median is about 0.5 s with spikes of several seconds (up to about 9 s in one day), because the line is shared and, after the quota, throttled to about 5 Mbit/s (see the Router and WAN board). A band that stays high for hours is the line. No alert rule watches latency.

panels.title: Public probe time by phase (selected probe)
panels.description: Where the time of the selected public probe goes: DNS resolve, TCP connect, TLS handshake, server processing, transfer. The phases add up to the request, so they are stacked. Pick the probe with the Public probe filter. A tall connect or TLS band is the line or Cloudflare; a tall processing band is the origin.

panels.title: Health URL state
panels.description: Whether each health URL from inventory/lab.yaml answered as expected (rule HttpProbeFailed: 5 minutes; 2xx, or any answer for the management UIs that use the http_any module). Green = answers, red = fails while the host may still ping.

panels.title: HTTP status per health URL
panels.description: The last HTTP status code of each probe. 200 is healthy. 401 is expected on kubeletto-registry-auth (an anonymous token request) and on the management UIs that use the http_any module; a 5xx or 0 (no answer) is a failing service. Read it together with the state chart, which applies each probe's own success rule.

panels.title: Probe time per health URL
panels.description: Total time of each health probe: duration of the services' front doors. Lab URLs answer in a few ms to tens of ms; the switch UI is the slowest (about 170 ms, a small embedded server). A sustained rise on one line is that service slowing down. No alert rule watches latency.

panels.title: Request time by phase (average over the selected URLs)
panels.description: Average time of each HTTP phase across the selected health URLs: resolve, connect, TLS, processing, transfer. The phases add up to the request, so they are stacked; select one host to see only that host. A growing TLS band is a slow certificate handshake, a growing processing band is a slow service.

panels.title: Certificate days left
panels.description: Days until the TLS certificate each probe saw expires, for every HTTPS health URL and the public endpoints. Anything beyond a year reads 365 (the PBS certificates run for centuries). Green over 30 days, orange under 30, red under 14. No alert rule watches this yet, so check it on the weekly review.

panels.title: Internet and DNS probes: up or down
panels.description: Ping to 1.1.1.1 (internet-cloudflare) and 8.8.8.8 (internet-google) and the hEX resolver's lookup of a public name. InternetDown fires when both pings fail for 3 minutes; DnsResolverFailing when the lookup fails for 3 minutes. Red on one internet line only is that resolver, not the uplink.

panels.title: Internet and DNS availability, 7 days
panels.description: Share of the last 7 days each probe answered. Green is 99.9 % or better, orange under 99.9 %, red under 99 %. The household line is the weak link: a few tenths of a percent below 100 (tens of minutes a week) shows an uplink blip even when no alert fired (they need 3 minutes).

panels.title: Internet round-trip time
panels.description: Ping round-trip time to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8 over the household line: 15 to 30 ms at the moment. A sustained rise while the line is busy is queueing on the uplink (compare the WAN throughput on the Router and WAN board). A line that is missing here is down in the state chart. No alert rule watches latency.

panels.title: DNS lookup time (hEX resolver)
panels.description: How long the hEX takes to answer the probe's lookup of a public name (the request phase): a few ms normally, with rare spikes of seconds (up to about 2 s in one day). A sustained rise means the hEX is waiting on its upstream resolver. probe_dns_lookup_time_seconds is deliberately not used: it times blackbox resolving the resolver's own address (microseconds), not the resolver. Rule DnsResolverFailing fires on failure, not on slowness.
